pageCache.text:
Discover Our Prep Curriculum with Creative Curriculum Design
The Prep curriculum is shaped by the principles of the Cambridge Primary Curriculum (CPC)—emphasising global understanding, critical thinking, and inquiry-led learning. These foundations support our commitment to active, engaging, and creative education that nurtures curiosity, confidence, and a love of learning.
While inspired by CPC, our curriculum is enriched by diverse influences and innovative practices tailored to the needs of our pupils. Core subjects—English, Maths, and Science—are aligned to the English National Curriculum, ensuring academic rigour and allowing us to benchmark progress against national expectations for learning progress. This blended approach prepares students to thrive in a fast-changing world.
At Wotton House Prep, our co-curricular programme plays a vital role in delivering a truly holistic education. Co-curricular activities are structured learning experiences that take place outside the core academic timetable, yet are deeply connected to our values and educational mission.
We run these activities to help children grow in confidence, creativity, and independence—developing the personal and social skills they need to thrive. From sport and the arts to outdoor learning and service opportunities, our co-curricular offer encourages teamwork, curiosity, and resilience. These experiences aren’t extras—they are part of how we nurture well-rounded learners ready to flourish in a changing world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Personalised Schooling | Wotton House International School
pageCache.text:
Specialist Prep Team
'Wellingtonia' Class
Our Prep school is led by Mary, who is also part of the Wotton House School leadership team. She works alongside Hannah, Nicola, and Jamie-Lee — a close-knit team of teachers who specialise in guiding children aged 5–11 through these key years. Together they teach English and Maths, track each child’s progress, and bring learning to life with experiences like the annual residential trip, weekly Farm School, and dramatic productions such as the Christmas concert.
Our pupils also benefit from specialist teachers in Science, Technology, and PSHE, giving them a broad, exciting education beyond the core curriculum.

Junior Curriculum
The Year 7–9 (Junior Curriculum) provides a strong academic foundation while encouraging creativity, curiosity, and confidence. Students follow a single, balanced pathway that combines core subjects with creative, physical, and holistic opportunities.
The timetable is fully personalised to reflect each learner’s strengths, needs, and aspirations. Adaptations to content, pace, and delivery ensure learning that fits—through targeted support, extension, or alternative arrangements.
This approach equips students for the specialist pathways of Years 10 and 11, while building the skills and self-belief needed for success in the wider world.
'Year 7 was exciting because I got to try so many new subjects and join Jewellery making elective club.
I liked making friends with some of the older kids who were kind and funny'
'In Year 8 I liked best learning about Neolithic farming with Mr Swann. We went out to the farm every week to plant and grow things with my friends. It was hard work, but it was also really cool and fun.'
'In Year 9 we got to run the Sports Leaders project with Mr Vaughan. It was fun to mix sports with learning and to give Prep kids the chance to play and get better at sports like rounders and football'

Special Educational Needs
We believe Special Educational Needs and personalised learning go hand in hand. Personalised learning means shaping lessons so every child can thrive — whether that’s giving extra challenge, adapting how we teach, or offering extra support.
For children with identified SEN, this simply becomes a more focused version of what we already do, with extra strategies or resources to help them succeed. Our aim is always the same: to make learning accessible and enjoyable for every child.

Senior Curriculum
​In Years 10 and 11, students follow one of two main pathways – IB MYP or the IGCSE Composite pathway – each offering a different balance of subject focus and learning approach. These years are highly personalised, and it is common for elements of either pathway to be adapted or blended to create learning that fits each student’s needs. At the end of Year 9, teachers provide clear guidance to help students and families choose the pathway that offers the best fit for their strengths, interests, and future aspirations.

At Wotton House, our starting point has always been the needs of our students rather than the requirements of an inspection framework. As we have grown, we have become increasingly skilled at demonstrating that highly personalised education can also meet the rigorous expectations of external inspectorates. For us, inspection is not simply about compliance—it is an opportunity to validate, refine and continually improve our practice.

pageCache.text:
Prep School
Our small classes allow for exceptional pastoral care and truly personalised learning. We blend expert teaching with innovative technology, outdoor education, and farm school to engage children actively with the world around them.
Unlike traditional prep schools, our focus isn’t on exam preparation at age 11. Instead, we nurture curiosity, confidence, and a lifelong love of learning—developing the thinking skills and learning habits children need to thrive in senior school and beyond.
All of this is delivered at fees that offer outstanding value.
